testcase.name: the full D.1 parity corpus (648 assertions) is green THROUGH the shim — no arg, byte of output, or exit code lost
.github#1818: the diagnostic names an early failure that a tail -25 of the same log would have hidden, plus the inner run's summary
tier 1: FSGG_COORD_ENGINE_BIN is honoured — the named engine runs and its version prints through
tier 1: an explicit-but-missing bin is REFUSED (exit 69), naming it — never a silent fall-back
tier 2: with the env unset, the shim resolves an engine from source and answers (version 0.58.1.0)
refusal: an unresolvable environment exits non-zero (69) with advice — never a silent green no-op (#266)
staleness: an engine NEWER than its src/ is silent — no warning on the happy path, and the FIXTURE is what ran
staleness: a stale engine WARNS on a read verb ('who') — and still runs, exit code intact
staleness: a stale engine REFUSES the board write 'release' (exit 69) — the engine never ran
staleness: a stale engine REFUSES the board write 'set-field' (exit 69) — the engine never ran
staleness: a stale engine REFUSES the board write 'done' (exit 69) — the engine never ran
staleness: a stale engine REFUSES the board write 'claim' (exit 69) — the engine never ran
staleness: with NO source present, even a board write is unaffected — nothing to be stale against
staleness: an explicit FSGG_COORD_ENGINE_BIN is honoured silently — an instruction, not a hint
partition: every verb the engine advertises (49) is classified by the shim — a new verb cannot slip in unguarded
partition: every verb the shim classifies is a verb the engine actually has — no set has rotted past the surface it describes
partition: the three sets are DISJOINT — no verb is classified twice, so there is one answer per verb
partition: shim membership matches every engine writes contract

staleness: every write verb the shim declares is refused on a stale engine — add adopt child claim done flush heartbeat intake release review room say set-field set-paths take widen delivery delivery-route graphql next reap reconcile

staleness: every read verb the shim declares still runs (with a warning) on a stale engine — batch board body-edits bootstrap budget command-contract cycle decide diff-audit driver facts field-id followup inbox issues item-id landable lanes
staleness: stale delivery-route validate FS.GG.SDD#70 receipt.json warns and runs as a delivery-route read
staleness: stale delivery-route show FS.GG.SDD#70 warns and runs as a delivery-route read
staleness: delivery-route record is refused before its receipt write
staleness: 'widen' is REFUSED on a stale engine (exit 69) — the touch-set pair cannot drift apart again
staleness: 'set-paths' is REFUSED on a stale engine (exit 69) — the touch-set pair cannot drift apart again
staleness: a verb the shim classifies NOWHERE is REFUSED on a stale engine (exit 69) — unknown write-ness fails closed
staleness: '--help' is not a verb and is not refused — the exemption is the grammar, not a list
staleness: '-h' is not a verb and is not refused — the exemption is the grammar, not a list
staleness: '--version' is not a verb and is not refused — the exemption is the grammar, not a list
staleness: a BARE invocation (empty verb) is not matched as a board write — it warns and reaches the engine
.github#1572: a newer generated 'obj/**/*.fs' is NOT source — the board write lands, exit 0
.github#1572: a newer '.fs' under 'bin/' is build OUTPUT, not input — the board write lands
.github#1572: a newer HAND-WRITTEN src/**/*.fs still REFUSES the board write, and is the file NAMED
.github#1549: a checkout LEVEL with its upstream is silent — a board write lands, exit 0
.github#1549: BEHIND on a non-engine path is not stale — the bar is drift in the engine's own source trees
.github#1549: a checkout BEHIND main under the engine's source trees REFUSES 'widen' (exit 69) — the engine never ran
.github#1549: the refusal names WHICH checkout to update and WHICH build to re-run, by absolute path
.github#1549: a READ on a behind-main checkout WARNS and still runs — reads warn, writes refuse, unchanged
.github#1549: a CURRENT worktree resolving a BEHIND shared engine is refused, and the SHARED checkout is the one named (#931 + #1549)
.github#1549: the remedy AS PRINTED (git -C $CL merge --ff-only refs/remotes/origin/main) clears the refusal on a checkout that is on a branch
.github#1664: a DETACHED checkout behind main still REFUSES the write — the state is reachable here
.github#1664: the remedy AS PRINTED (git -C $CL merge --ff-only refs/remotes/origin/main) fast-forwards a DETACHED checkout and clears the refusal
.github#1549: a checkout with NO origin remote has no default branch to be behind — no verdict, not a refusal
.github#1549: an unanswerable staleness question REFUSES the board write (exit 69) — it does not read as freshness (#266)
.github#1549: a no-verdict still PERMITS a read — the refusal is scoped to writes, as #929 scoped it
.github#1549: an engine-source pathspec that matches NO commit is a no-verdict, not a zero — the guard refuses to report on an unwatched subject
#1586: 'scripts/fsgg-coord' IS a kit row — the split's premise still holds (if this ever flips the split is moot, not passing)
#1586: the guard module has NO kit row, so the packer cannot stage it — a partition edit is now a .github commit, not a republish + 7-receiver fan-out
#1586: a source build with NO guard module beside the shim REFUSES the board write (exit 69) and NAMES the module — an absent guard is not a clean bill of health (#266)
#1586: with NO source build, the missing guard module is never asked for — the receivers' shape resolves (or refuses) exactly as before

#1615: the engine tool manifest has NO kit row (ADR-0068), so an engine version bump is a .github commit and a per-receiver Renovate PR — not a republish + 7-receiver fan-out. With leg (a), #1586's criterion 5 is now MEETABLE
#1615/#1077: the engine-manifest sweep is present in repos-audit.sh — the invariant the kit row used to buy by construction is asserted against every receiver's tree (AC2)
.github#2653: a worktree carrying an INCIDENTAL engine build writes the board through the SHARED checkout's current engine — the build no longer shadows tier 2b
.github#2653: with the shared engine REMOVED, g1's condition no longer holds — the leg examines a real fall-through target rather than passing over nothing
.github#2653: a worktree that AUTHORS engine source of its own keeps tier 2a — and a genuinely stale deliberate build is still REFUSED, with neither engine reached
.github#2653: the worktree-local refusal names the worktree, says it is not the shared checkout, and reports the observed reason tier 2a preferred that build
.github#2653: with the SHARED engine stale, an incidental-but-CURRENT local build is kept — resolution only ever moves toward an engine that answers 'current'
.github#2653: with no default-branch ref to answer the authorship question, the caller's own build is still preferred and still guarded — an unanswerable probe changes nothing

.github#2653: a FAILING dirt probe (corrupt index, exit 128, empty stdout) is read as unanswerable, not as a clean tree — the caller's own build is kept, no engine runs, and the refusal says the question could not be answered
precedence: a global tool on PATH does NOT preempt the source build — .github never runs the feed (ADR-0034 decision 2)
precedence: a global tool cannot route a board write around the STALE guard (exit 69) — #929's guard is REACHABLE (#1018)
precedence: tier 1 still outranks the source build — an explicit bin is an instruction, and the operator's escape hatch
precedence: a receiver (no source build) still resolves the global tool — the reorder keys on the BUILD, not a repo name
tier 2b: an item worktree with NO build resolves the SHARED checkout's engine — not exit 69 (#931)
tier 2b: a FRESH worktree is not STALE — the guards measure the shared tree's own src/↔build, so board writes still land (#931)
tier 2b: a genuinely STALE shared engine still REFUSES a board write driven from a worktree — the guard measures, it does not skip
tier 2b: a DIRTY shared checkout warns the worktree worker whose claims that WIP decides (#709)
tier 2b: a worktree that HAS its own build runs it — the fallback is after 2a, never before it (#931)

.github#2471: a STALE tier-2a build beside a CURRENT shared checkout names ITS OWN toplevel, says plainly it is not the shared one (naming /tmp/tmp.4ND4hrkqc8/shared), and does not send the reader to merge main into a feature branch
dirtiness: a COMMITTED checkout is silent — a built, gitignored bin/ is not dirt (#709)
dirtiness: a dirty checkout WARNS on the board write 'claim' and STILL RUNS it — warn, never refuse (#709)
dirtiness: STAGED work still warns — 'status --porcelain' sees what 'diff --quiet' cannot
dirtiness: an UNTRACKED source file warns — it is not on main either
dirtiness: a dirty 'scripts/fsgg-coord' warns and is NAMED — it ends up inside the engine as surely as a .fs does
dirtiness: a dirty 'Directory.Build.props' warns and is NAMED — it ends up inside the engine as surely as a .fs does
dirtiness: a dirty 'Directory.Packages.props' warns and is NAMED — it ends up inside the engine as surely as a .fs does
dirtiness: a dirty 'global.json' warns and is NAMED — it ends up inside the engine as surely as a .fs does
dirtiness: the warning lists 5 paths and counts the remainder — '7 path(s)', 'and 2 more'
dirtiness: an explicit FSGG_COORD_ENGINE_BIN never consults the guard — tier 1 execs first
dirtiness: a kit author's DIRTY worktree is exempt — §2's sanctioned flow is not the violation it enforces (#709)
dirtiness: 'status.showUntrackedFiles=no' cannot blind the guard — the probe forces its own scope (#1043)
dirtiness: a checkout with NO HEAD has no baseline to be dirty against — no verdict, not a false alarm
